timing_definitions.elapsed_hours_to_last_completed_step: Timestamp difference from the first 'Sample data for step 1 started' line to the selected completed-step metric. Includes intervening pauses and restarts; excludes initialization before step 1 and activity after the endpoint.
timing_definitions.read_plus_train_hours: Sum of time/read_experience plus time/train_step for the specified scalar records. These sequential trainer-loop intervals exclude some startup, checkpoint, restart and other unlogged overhead; they are not GPU busy time.
timing_definitions.deduplicated_trajectory_work: One retained record per step; suitable for plotting a final learning trajectory. Discarded computations do not become free and are counted separately.
timing_definitions.raw_logged_work: All completed-step scalar records, including superseded repetitions. This still does not constitute total metered or billed consumption.
timing_definitions.eight_gpu_hours_from_read_plus_train: Illustrative fixed-allocation accounting: read_plus_train_hours × 8 GPUs. Not measured utilization, energy, billing, or a claim that all eight GPUs were busy.
timing_definitions.timestamp_note: Timestamps are preserved in the server log's local notation. Timezone offsets are not encoded in these logs.
timing_definitions.update_actor_us_per_token_ratio_of_sums: sum(time/update_actor) / sum(perf/total_num_tokens) × 1e6; a token-weighted aggregate of training-update time only.
timing_definitions.update_actor_us_per_token_mean_of_step_r: Arithmetic mean of each step's time/update_actor / perf/total_num_tokens × 1e6. This differs from the ratio of sums and must not be mixed with it.

hardware.basis: Historical experiment reports and documented machine configuration; not inferred from the number of trainable parameters.

processing.deduplication_rule: Retain the last scalar record for each trainer step to reconstruct the final training trajectory. Account for all original records separately when summing logged work.

verl.endpoint_note: The log contains completed steps 1–133. Step 134 starts after the last metric but has no completed-step metric; that unfinished work is excluded. The tutorial selects checkpoint 100 retrospectively, but the actual run continued through 133.

lora32_speed.endpoint_note: The final run restored checkpoints 10, 90 and 100 during concurrency changes. Earlier computations of steps 101 and 102 were discarded from the final trajectory but remain included in raw_logged_work.

score_semantics.meaning: Mean final reward over the experience records in a training batch. Each experience is one dialogue/environment turn; it is not an equal-weight mean over completed episodes.
score_semantics.reward_propagation: The episode's final reward is assigned to each of its experience records. Longer episodes can contribute more records, and replay/batch sampling changes their representation.
score_semantics.interpretation: The curves can share a training-batch reward axis, with differences in sampling and asynchronous data flow disclosed. Do not relabel (score + 0.1) / 1.1 as an equal-weight episode success rate.

evaluation_boundary.verl_checkpoint_100: A matched held-out evaluation was not found in the inspected baseline reports, tutorial, or the final LoRA comparison log. The baseline report lists checkpoint evaluation as future work.
evaluation_boundary.scope: The final LoRA comparison log evaluates optimized LoRA and original LoRA only. Absence here does not prove no other uninspected evaluation exists.
evaluation_boundary.no_early_stop_claim: Training scores around step 130 do not establish the best stopping point or the held-out accuracy of that checkpoint.

v3_full_parameter_scope.note: The V3 TuFT full-parameter correctness run is separate from the tutorial's verl baseline. Its log later includes speed-tuning work and restores; it is not used as the main cost comparator here.
v3_full_parameter_scope.report_discrepancy: The older report's step 66–83 comparison does not match the inspected trainer logs or TensorBoard records. No quantitative correctness-equivalence conclusion is imported from that table.

limitations: These are observations from different historical runs, not a single-variable benchmark of LoRA versus full-parameter training.
Learning rate, backend, sampling concurrency, asynchronous sampling, sequence lengths and other implementation conditions differ.
A common trainer-step count does not ensure equal token volume, equal sampled episodes or equal model quality.
Both experiments reserved eight GPUs; reduced trainable-parameter count alone does not demonstrate lower hardware requirements or lower end-to-end cost.
No GPU billing records, utilization-integrated device hours, power measurements, or common-quality stopping comparison are available in this evidence.
All figures were recomputed from existing records without rerunning training or evaluation.
Private machine paths and run identifiers are intentionally omitted.
